Probing Water at Interfaces with Vibrational Spectroscopy

Navigation text

Abstract: Water at interfaces governs processes ranging from atmospheric chemistry to electrocatalysis. In this work, sum-frequency generation spectroscopy and ultrafast infrared pump-probe measurements are used to characterise the hydrogen-bond network of water at charged surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations complement the experiments and show that interfacial water reorients within picoseconds. These results clarify how surface charge controls the structure of interfacial water and suggest design rules for electrode materials in water splitting.
